full_judgment:
Abdul Awal J: Mr AM Mahbub Uddin, learned Advocate for the petitioner, drawing our attention to paragraph Nos. 17 and 18 of the revision application, submits that there is no evidence or statement or any implication against the petitioner in' the Case CR No. 08-369-RJL in the Columbia District Court in USA filed by the US Government against Siemens Bangladesh Limited. Whereas, the involvement of the petitioner mentioned in the charge-sheet referring the above case in USA is without any basis. He further submits that in case of schedule offence under the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 committed outside of Bangladesh two sanctions are necessary i.e. one from the Government under section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to investigate into the case and another from the Anti-Corruption Commission under section 32 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 for submission of the charge-sheet. Only one sanction is necessary under section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to investigate into the case in case of non-schedule offence of the Anti- Corruption Commission Act, 2004; as section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act remains silent as to such sanction of the Government. He submits that due to silence of the other procedural matter in the Criminal Law Amendment Act, how far the Code of Criminal Procedure will be applicable to proceed with the Special Case. He lastly submits that there is no prima-facie reason to lodge the instant case against the petitioner after the judgment and order dated 27-8-2003 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 4965 of 2003. No other authority raise any question regarding obtaining the work order from BTTB after aforesaid judgment. 

 Md Faruque (M. Faruque) J: In this revisional application under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, accused- petitioner Mrs. Mafruza Sultana challenged the order dated 4-9-2012 rejecting the application under section 13 of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2002 in Metro Special Case No. 138 of 2012 corresponding to GR Case No. of 2011 arising out of Gulshan Police Station Case No. 45 dated 16-8-2011, now pending before the learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka. 

 12. It has been further stated that the prosecution have to follow the procedure laid down in section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the offence committed outside of Bangladesh and that a sanction from the government was necessary to enquire to the offence as per provision of the section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and that the offence committed cannot be tried in Bangladesh and that it has not been mentioned in the FIR or charge-sheet under which law the alleged offence is an offence in Singapore. 

 13. Heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner and perused the supplementary affidavits filed by the accused-petitioner dated 10-12-2012 and 8-1-2013. It has been stated in the supplementary affidavits that section 28(2) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, the provision of the Criminal Law amendment Act, 1958 except the provision of sub-section 6 of section 6 of the Criminal law Amendment Act, 1958 shall be applicable for trial and disposal of the appeal in respect of the offence under this Act, and the schedule of the Act. Section 28(3) of the Anti- Corruption Commission Act, 2004 in case of any conflict between any provision of Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and provision of this Act, the provisions of this Act shall prevail. Further it has been stated that section 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 shall in so far as they are not inconsistent with this Act, apply to the proceeding of the Court of Special Judge. However, the case against the accused-petitioner is under the schedule of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act and therefore, the case shall be triable by the Special Judge. It has been stated that prosecution has to follow the procedure laid down in section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for the offence committed outside Bangladesh in accordance with the Amendment Act, 1958 and that the prosecution must obtain the sanction of the government for making any enquiry or trial if any offence committed in Singapore. It has been further stated that the legality or illegality regarding the declaration of responsive or non-responsive of any participants of the tender was decided by the judgment and order dated 27-8-2003 in Writ Petition No. 4965 of 2003. Nobody can raise any question regarding obtaining the work order from BTTB after the aforesaid judgment and order. 

 17. Hon'ble Appellate Division in the afore- said decision decided that legislature has consciously included the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 in the schedule to the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and also included the offences under the Ain, 2002 in the schedule to the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, whereby any enquiry investigation, lodging of the complaint, conducting of prosecution before the Special Judge and holding of trial exclusively by the Special Judge have been mandatorily required under the provisions of Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and the same provision is equally applicable in the case of the offences under the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2009. Furthermore, their Lordships decided that since the alleged offences were committed during the operation of the Money Laundering Ain, 2002, punishment for the said offence as provided under Chapter IV of the said Ain be applicable and there is no bar to hold the trial of the case under the provisions of the Anti- Corruption Commission Act, 2004 for the commission of the offence alleged to have been committed under the Ain of 2002 treating the case as one instituted under the Ain of 2002 and that from a clear reading of the FIR, Investigation Report and materials on record, a prima-facie case under section 2(ট) (আ) (ই)and section 13 of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 has been disclosed and the prosecution may proceed under Anti-Corruption Commission Ordinance in accordance with law. 

 19. Sections 4(4), 6(1) and the Schedule of The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 read as follows: 

 "The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. 

 Provided that [notwithstanding anything in any of the proceeding sections of this Chapter no charge as to any such offence shall he inquired into in [Bangladesh] [except with the sanction of the Government]: 

 22. In the revisional application virtually the legality of the proceeding of the case has been challenged before us. Hon'ble Appellate Division in a similar case of "Tarique Rahman vs Bangladesh" reported in 63 DLR (AD) 18 decided that legislature has consciously included the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 in the schedule to the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 as well as in the schedule to the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and that any enquiry, investigation, lodging of the complaint, conducting of the prosecution before the Special Judge and holding of trial of the case exclusively by the Special Judge have been made required under the provisions of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and the same provision is equally applicable in the case of the offences under the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain. Furthermore, I have already discussed that their Lordships found the disclosure of the prima-facie case in the FIR, Investigation Report and other materials on record under sections 2(ট) (আ)(ই) and section 13 of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain against the accused-persons of the said case and the prosecution can proceed, with the case in accordance with law under the Money Laundering Ain, 2002 since the alleged offence were committed during the operation of the Ain, 2002. 

 (২) এই আইনের অধীন ও উহার তফসিলে বর্ণিত অপরাধ সমূহের বিচার ও আপীল নিষ্পত্তির ক্ষেত্রে The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 এর section 6 এর sub-section (5) এবং sub-section (6) এর বিধান ব্যতীত অন্যান্য বিধানাবলি প্রযোজ্য হইবে। 

 (৩) The Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 এর কোন বিধান এই আইনের কোন বিধানের সহিত অসঙ্গতিপূর্ণ হইলে এই আইনের বিধান কার্যকর হইবে। 

 24. According to section 32(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 or in subsisting any other law, a Special Judge will not take cognizance of any offence under this Act, 2004 without the sanction of the Anti-Corruption Commission and in this case admittedly the Investigating Officer submitted the investigation report along with the sanction of the Anti-Corruption Commission. Neither in the Anti-Corruption Act, 2004 nor in the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, has any provision been made requiring the sanction of the Government to take cognizance or enquire into the offences under these Acts by a Special Judge. As per sub-section 4 of section 4 of the Criminal I Law Amendment Act, 1958 offences being committed outside Bangladesh, shall be deemed to have been committed within the territorial limits of the jurisdiction of the Special Judge in Bangladesh in which the person, committing the offence is found or was ordinarily residing before he left Bangladesh. 

 25. According to section 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, shall, in so far as they are not inconsistent with this Act 1958, apply to the proceedings of the Court of a Special Judge. From the above made discussions it is found that the provision of section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 is inconsistent with the provision of section (4) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 inasmuch as with the provision of section 32 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004. 

 26. For explaining the proviso of section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 that no charge as to any such offence shall be enquired into in Bangladesh except with the sanction of the Government, I searched from the Maxwell sand NS Bindra's Interpretation of Statutes, it may he discussed that the aforesaid provision has been made without expressly declaring about what shall be the consequence of non-compliance of the proviso, it has not been said that for non-compliance, that is for want of sanction of the Government, the proceeding will be invalid or null and void and in absence of the declaration of any consequence for non-compliance, the very proviso is not mandatory. It is merely directory. 

 27. Considering the above mentioned interpretations it is found that the proviso of section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not mandatory. For the reasons, discussed above and in terms of sections 4(4) and 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and section 32 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, this provision has got no manner of application in the present case. 

 29. Accordingly, in my view sanction of the Government is not required to proceed with the present case. The proceeding is being dealt with in accordance with law. 

 34. The accused petitioner has filed this replication under section 10(1A) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 challenging the order dated 4-9-2012 passed by the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka in Metro Special Case No. 138 of 2012 arising out of GR Case No. 88 of 2011 corresponding to Gulshan Police Station Case No.45 dated 16-8-2011 taking cognizance against the accused petitioner under section 13 of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002. 

 43. AM Mahbub Uddin, the learned Advocate for the accused petitioner, submits that the prosecution has not complied with the conditions as laid down in section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before initiating the instant case. The prosecution should have obtained the sanction of the Government before making any enquiry or trial as the offence alleged to have been committed outside the Bangladesh i.e. in Singapore. In the instant case no Government; sanction as required in section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was obtained to proceed with the case. The Court in taking cognizance wrongly came to a finding that only the sanction of Anti-Corruption Commission is enough to proceed with the case and failed to appreciate that the said sanction under section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not alike the sanction under section 12 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004. The alleged offence has not been committed in Bangladesh and therefore, a sanction from the Government is necessary to inquire into the present case as per provision of section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure; but no sanction was accorded by the Government to inquire in to the said matter. 

 45. Mr Mahbub Uddin referring to the case of Tarique Rahman vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 63 DLR (AD) 18 further submits that in the said case the Appellate Division having found prima-facie case under section 2 (ট)(আ)(অ) and section 13 of the Money Laundering Ain, 2002 against the accused of the said case held that prosecution may proceed with the case against the accused persons in accordance with law, if so advised; but in the instant case from the plain reading of the FIR and the charge-sheet it does not appear that any prima-facie case has been dis- closed under the Money Laundering Ain, 2002 or Ain, 2009 and, as such, taking cognizance into the case is absolutely illegal. He also submits that in the FIR it has been mentioned that in a Criminal Case held in District Court of Columbia, USA Siemens was found guilty as they admitted to have bribed various persons of Bangladesh in order to get a contract of BTCL but the present accused petitioner was not a party to the said case; even no finding has been given against the present accused petitioner. In this connection he has drawn my attention to paragraph 17 of the application, where the relevant portion of the judgment passed by the District Court of Columbia, USA has been quoted. 

 63. Mr Mahbub Uddin has raised another issue to the effect that the Ordinance No. VII of 2007 and Ordinance No. VIII of 2007 by which the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 was incorporated in the schedule of the Anti- Corruption Commission Act, 1958 were not placed before the parliament as per the provision of Article 93 of the Constitution of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh and those Ordinance were not approved by the parliament and, as such, the said Ordinance died their natural death upon expire of 30 days of the first meeting of the 9th parliament. As such it cannot be said that Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 is no more in the schedule of Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and thus, the proceeding under the Ain of 2002 is absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction by the Special Judge. 

 "I t is to be noticed that Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2009 has given effect on and from 15th April, 2008 corresponding to 2nd Baishak, 1413 BS that is before the election of 9th Parliament and its 1st meeting. Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2009 had been repealed by Money Laundering Protirodh Ordinance, 2008 on 15- 4-2003 with a provision of saving clause; Money Laundering Protirodh Ordinance 2008 was also repealed by the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2009 with another saving clause in section 31 (2) of the Ain and there is a continuity of legislation in between the Ain of 2002 and Ain of 2009 and thus, the Ordinances in question have got no manner of application after enactment of Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2009 which has come into force before the constitution of the 9th Parliament and its first meeting and, as such, the question whether the Ordinance Nos. VII and VIII 2007, by which the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 was incorporated in the schedule of Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 respectively, were not placed before the first meeting of 9th Parliament and was not approved by the Parliament as per provision of Article 93 (2) and (4) of the Constitution thus it is deemed that Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 is no more in the schedule of Anti-Corruption Commission Act of 2004 and Criminal Law Amendment Act of 1958 has also become irrelevant which has got no substance. It is also a redundant issue." 

 "Accordingly, inquiry, investigation lodging of complaint and conduct of prosecution of the cases and holding of the trial in respect of those case under the Ain of 2002 shall proceed under the Provision of Anti- Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and that in the case of any conflict with the provision of Ain, 2002 the provision of Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 shall prevail though the Ain of 2002 was repealed by the Ordinance, 2008 keeping similar provision as of section 3 (ক) in section 9 of the Ordinance, 2008 and also in section 9 of the Ain, 2009." 

 68. Keeping in mind the above decisions and observation of the Appellate Division let us now consider the submission of Mr Mahbubuddin whether section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure will be applicable in this particular case that is whether sanction of Government is mandatory for inquiry into this case and to hold trial; though the learned Special Judge has kept the matter open. 

 69. In the above cases it is the consistent view of the Appellate Division that since the alleged offence have been committed during the operation of Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002, its punishment would be dealt with under the provision of the said Ain of2002; but the procedure in respect of the inquiry, investigation, conducting prosecution and holding trial shall be governed under the provision of Anti-Corruption Commission Act of 2004 and Criminal Law Amendment Act of 1958. 

 70. In view of the above decisions and observation of the Appellate Division there is no scope to hold that the sanction of the Government is mandatory to make inquiry of the offence of the present case as per provision of section 183 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 73. This provision of law clearly and consciously ousted the power of sanction of the Government keeping the spirit that Anti-Corruption Commission being a statutory body, it should be free from any interference by the Government section 20 (1) of the Anti-Corruption Act, 2004 is as under: 

 "and that in case of conflict with the provisions of the Ain 2002, the provision of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and the Criminal Law Amendment Art, 1958 shall prevail though the Ain of2002 was repealed by the ordinance of 2008 keeping similar provision as of section 3(ক) of the Ain of 2002 in the section 9 of the Ordinance of 2008 and also in section 9 of the Ain of 2009" 

 (২) এই আইনের অধীন অপরাধ সমূহ Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 (Act XL of 1958) এর section 3 এর অধীন নিযুক্ত স্পেশান জজ কর্তৃক বিচার্য হইবে। 

 (৩) এই আইনের অধীন অপরাধ সমূহের তদন্ত বিচার ও সংশ্লিষ্ট অন্যান্য বিষয়ে এই আইনের বিধানাবলীর সহিত বিরোধের ক্ষেত্রে দূর্নীতি দমন কমিশন আইন ২০০৪ এবং Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 এর বিধানবলী প্রধান্য পাইবে।” 

 81. All the provisions of law mentioned above speak that the offence of the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002, Ordinance of 2008 and Ain of 2009 deemed to be (অপরাধ গন্য) the schedule offence of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and triable by the Special Judge under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. As such the question whether Money Laundering Protirodh Ain 2002 or 2009 has been included in the schedule has got no substance and it is irrelevant. Law clearly provides that the offence under Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 or Ain, 2009 is deemed to be (অপরাধ গন্য) in the schedule of Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and the offence will be tried by the Special Judge under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. As such the provision of section 20(1) and 32 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and sections 4(4) and 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 will come in to play in this particular case. 

 83. And section 4(4) of the Criminal Law Amendment 1958 is as follows: 

 85. In view of the above provisions of law section 188 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not at all applicable in this particular case; rather it is inconsistent with the provisions of sections 20(1) and 32 of the Anti-Corruption Act, 2004 and sections 4(4) and 6( 1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958.
